subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & cost levers — Nova Retail (P.O.C. next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@novaretail.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & cost levers — recap + next steps

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Great to meet with you both today. Quick recap from our discovery on latency/throughput requirements and the recommended levers to hit your SLOs. Please see the attached worksheet (performance-slo-worksheet.xlsx) where we captured the numbers below.

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Latency target: 200ms p95 for user-facing recommendations (streamed response preferred)
- Concurrency: ~40-60 concurrent users at peak (estimate: 50)
- Throughput: ~120k tokens/day (avg), with spikes during promotions
- Streaming: yes — client expects token-by-token streaming for progressive UI

Initial recommended levers to evaluate (high-level):
1) Continuous batching and request bundling to increase GPU utilization while preserving tail latency
2) KV/prefix caching for repeated context (product catalog snippets) to avoid re-computation
3) Quantization profile: int8/4-bit options for moderate quality tradeoff — Rishi to propose concrete perf delta
4) Model variants: smaller decoder for short responses, full model for long-form outputs; automatic routing by intent

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- Redwood runs a short perf POC with your representative prompt set (we'll need ~50 sample prompts + typical context lengths) — target: characterize p95/throughput and cost estimates
- Rishi to share recommended quantization / batching config and expected latency bands
- Pricing/impact: I can put together a draft estimate for the POC and steady-state costs once we have perf numbers

Action items for Nova Retail: please reply with the prompt set + a short doc on typical context size and any must-stream fields.

Attaching: performance-slo-worksheet.xlsx (filled with the call notes) and a short PDF with options (redwood-slo-options.pdf).

Thanks —
Marissa
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

From: Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@novaretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@novaretail.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & cost levers — recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. Couple clarifications from our side:

- 200ms p95 is our stretch goal for the recommendation endpoint; 95th should be under 300ms initially.
- Streaming is important for the UX: we need token-level streaming for the first 300ms of the reply for perceived latency, then full payload is fine.
- Concurrency: 50 is a good working number. During promotions it could jump ~2x for short windows.

Can you also call out what the expected cost delta would be for enabling streaming + more aggressive batching? In particular we care about:
- Will continuous batching add tail latency risk?
- How much does KV/prefix caching typically save for product-catalog-heavy traffic?

We can share a 50-sample prompt set by EOD. Happy for Redwood to run the POC next week.

Ethan
Director, Product — Nova Retail
ethan.lu@novaretail.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Lu <ethan.lu@novaretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & cost levers — tech notes + POC plan

Ethan —

Thanks for the clarifications. Quick technical response + what we'll exercise in the POC. TL;DR: we can meet 200-300ms p95 with the right mix of streaming-friendly execution, moderate batching, and caching; cost tradeoffs depend on model/quantization choices.

What we'll test in the POC (1-week perf run):
- Baseline: full-precision model (fp16) with small batch windows (low-latency mode) — measure p50/p95 and tokens/sec
- Continuous batching profile: increase batch window to 20-340ms to improve GPU throughput; we'll measure tail effects and configure adaptive cutoffs so requests that hit p95 thresholds bypass batching
- Streaming instrumentation: we'll enable token streaming; measure initial-token latency (TTF) separately from full-response p95.
- KV/prefix caching: cache repeated product snippets; we'll simulate a 30% cache-hit rate to show savings in tokens and latency
- Quantization: test int8 and 4-bit profiles on candidate models; report quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE proxy + manual spot-check) and latency/cost delta
- Model routing: run a smaller variant for short responses and route to full model for longer replies; compute expected cost delta per 1k requests

Preliminary expectations (very coarse):
- Continuous batching (20-340ms window) can reduce per-token GPU cost by ~20-35% on typical sequences, with a <10% p95 increase if adaptive routing is used
- KV caching with a 30% hit can reduce token compute by ~25-30% for catalog-heavy prompts
- int8 quantization can reduce latency by ~15-25% and cost by ~20-30% with minor quality degradation on short-form responses; 4-bit yields larger savings but requires quality vetting

POC data we need from Nova:
- Representative prompt set (50-100) and typical context length distribution
- Baseline traffic shaping (peak concurrency windows) and any percentiles you care about beyond p95

Deliverables from Redwood POC:
- p50/p95/p99 latency matrix for streaming and non-streaming flows by model/config
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and per-1k-request cost estimate under each config
- Recommendation: config for production (batching/caching/quantization/model mix) and a short MOP (canary steps)

I'll upload a baseline perf plan and expected config knobs to the Drive folder (link in the thread). If this looks good we can schedule the perf run for next Tue/Wed.

Thanks —
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

I'll assemble the prompt set tonight. We can do Tue/Wed for the perf run if Redwood can commit to a primary contact during the test window.
